name: Outside-view engine: procedural-clock feasibility and reference-class hazards for 'by date' ladders
one_line: Compile each 'will X happen by date' market into the formal procedure that must complete, attach computed reference-class completion-time distributions, and sell rungs that are procedurally infeasible or priced above the outside-view hazard.
scope: (a) Procedure-graph extraction: steps, minimum durations and veto points for legislative calendars, treaty ratification, court scheduling, launch licensing, merger reviews and UNSC procedure. (b) Reference-class tournament: three or more candidate classes with computed base rates, not remembered ones, a red-team challenge on class membership, and a Fermi cross-check. This section should absorb the two duplicate reference-class variants now sitting in adversarial-debate-price-residual and sponsor-and-inform-niche-models. (c) Hazard term structure across the ladder: fit a constant or Weibull hazard and compare it with the market-implied one. Calendar spreads, rung k minus rung k-1, isolate 'happens in month k'. (d) Deadline-effect correction for bargaining events: agreements cluster right before the deadline, so the hazard is back-loaded, not constant. Present the negatives. Prompt-only base-rate tricks add little, so the edge has to come from the data pipeline. Insider flow dominates late in geopolitics ladders. 'Nothing ever happens' NO-buying already exists as a 987-star meme bot with no published PnL. Capital locks for months. Validation: on 60+ resolved by-date ladders after model cutoffs, compare market-implied and realised hazard by category and time-to-deadline. Then test whether 'minimum remaining procedural steps' improves log-loss over price alone. Score event-clustered.
why_it_matters: By-date ladders are among the most liquid non-sports books. The US-Iran final nuclear deal ladder has $17.84M volume, $404k liquidity and 8 rungs. The US-Russia nuclear deal ladder has $662k volume. The list handles these ladders only inside the geopolitics wargame entry, using simulation, the most biased tool in the band. The outside view is the best-documented human debiasing method. Mechanism: completion-time optimism, plus acquiescence. In Buehler 1994 only 13% finished by their own 50% date and 45% by their 99% date. Geopolitics is fee-free, so small hazard edges are tradable. The engine is also the natural home for the list's orphaned reference-class material.
flags: Geopolitics markets face insider-trading scrutiny. War-related contracts are restricted in some jurisdictions. NO positions on long ladders lock capital for months. This overlaps the behavioural-bias band if that band already has a 'YES-optimism / status-quo' entry, so check for duplication.
